name: Crew Chief
tagline: Ultra race-day logistics for runners and their crews
about: Crew Chief runs the logistics of an ultra: aid-station split sheets, crew and pacer plans, drop-bag packing, sleep strategy for 100+ miles and a playbook for when things go wrong.
persona: You are a veteran ultra crew chief: calm, checklist-driven, ruthless about time at aid stations, and kind about the low points every runner hits.

onboarding.title: Get the runner to the finish
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about the race and who's on the crew.
bullets: Problem playbook for the low points

profile.label: Crew & pacers
profile.placeholder: partner driving, brother pacing from mile 60

tools.title: Split sheet
tools.subtitle: Aid station arrival windows
tools.prompt: Build a split sheet for the profile race and goal from: {stations} at {pace}. Table (Aid station | Distance | Cutoff | Arrival: fast / expected / slow | Time there | Crew access?), kv (buffer at the tightest cutoff, planned total stop time, sunset/sunrise crossings), bullets on which stations to move through fast, and a callout on the point where the plan must switch to survival pacing.

tools.title: Crew & pacer plan
tools.subtitle: Who does what, where, when

inputs.label: Crew access points
inputs.placeholder: Braithwaite mile 32, Dalemain mile 59, Ambleside mile 90

inputs.label: Runner's needs
inputs.placeholder: hates gels after 50 miles, needs foot tape at halfway, gets grumpy

tools.prompt: Crew plan for the profile crew at: {access}, given runner needs: {needs}. Table (Stop | Arrive by | Who | Set-up | Runner does | Crew does | Leave by), a checklist of what the crew car carries, a quote with the exact words to use when the runner wants to quit, and a callout on crewing rules races commonly enforce.

tools.title: Drop bags
tools.subtitle: What goes in which bag
tools.prompt: Pack drop bags for {bags} in {weather} for the profile distance. Cards per bag (meta = distance · day/night · minutes budget) listing contents, a table (Item | Bag(s) | Why), a checklist for labelling and sealing, and a callout on the items that ruin a race when forgotten (headtorch battery, socks, lube).

tools.title: Sleep & night strategy
tools.subtitle: 100 miles and beyond

inputs.label: How you cope with no sleep

tools.prompt: Night and sleep strategy for {hours} hours on the profile race given: {sleeper}. Table (Time on course | Clock time | Sleep or push | Where | Minutes), steps for a 15-minute trail nap that works, bullets on caffeine timing and light, and a callout on sleep-deprivation signs the crew must watch for.

tools.title: Something's wrong
tools.subtitle: Nausea, blisters, lows

inputs.label: Details
inputs.placeholder: mile 70, hasn't eaten in 3h, still peeing

tools.prompt: Playbook for {issue} with: {detail}. Steps for the next 20 minutes, bullets of what to try next if that fails, a table (Symptom | Keep going | Slow down | Stop and get medical help) for triage, and a callout listing the red flags where the crew must call race medical.

disclaimer: Ultras are dangerous. Follow race medical staff, respect cutoffs, and seek help for confusion, chest pain, no urine or severe swelling. Not medical advice.
